open_points.subject: K-14 personal-data boundary for direct agent service access
open_points.text: “Personal data — values of class `personal_data` reach an agent only as digest and class; the owner alone reads them” and “An agent never receives a `personal_data` value” conflict with “the kernel neither gives nor checks [an agent's direct service access], and its personal-data promise (K-14) covers what the kernel itself returns.”
open_points.question: Is the personal-data guarantee limited to values returned through the kernel surface, allowing a microservice to disclose personal data directly to an agent under its own policy, or must direct agent access also preserve the digest-and-class-only rule?
options: Limit K-14 to the kernel surface and revise the unconditional actor and A07 statements
Require direct service access to enforce the same personal-data restriction
Forbid direct agent access to personal-data material
open_points.default_guess: Limit K-14 to the kernel surface, because the changed exclusion states that scope explicitly.
